question.worked_solution:
First, we note that $b=0$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

We multiply both sides of the equation by $b,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{b+5}{b}+\frac{b-7}{b} & =6 \\ b\cdot (\frac{b+5}{b}+\frac{b-7}{b}) & =b\cdot 6 \\ b\cdot \frac{b+5}{b}+b\cdot \frac{b-7}{b} & =b\cdot 6 \\ \cancel{b}\cdot \frac{b+5}{\cancel{b}}+\cancel{b}\cdot \frac{b-7}{\cancel{b}} & =b\cdot 6 \\ b+5+b-7 & =6b\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $b,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}b+5+b-7 & =6b \\ 2b-2 & =6b \\ -4b & =2 \\ b & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $b=0$ as a solution. However, since $b=-\frac{1}{2}\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $b=-\frac{1}{2}.$
